description:
Why Operation Market Garden Was COMPLETELY Avoidable

A little after seven on the evening of 20 September 1944, four British tanks rolled across the great road bridge at Nijmegen. Eleven kilometres up the same road, a few hundred British paratroopers had been holding the bridge at Arnhem for three days, waiting for exactly these tanks. The tanks stopped in the next village, Lent, and that night the men at Arnhem lost their bridge.
So — was Market Garden completely avoidable?

In this animated documentary we drive the one road from the Belgian border to Arnhem and paint every exit the Allies — and the Germans — could have taken. Each exit gets a date, a place and a person who could have taken it; hindsight doesn't count. A dispatcher keeps the clock against a timetable that promised Arnhem in two to three days.

We follow the summer of 1944 that made it look easy, the fuel crisis and the unopened port of Antwerp, Eisenhower and Montgomery's meeting at Brussels airport, the seven days of planning, the single daily lift and the drop zones 13 km from the bridge, the Type 22 radios, Field Marshal Model's hotel in Oosterbeek, the 9th and 10th SS Panzer divisions, the Lindemans 'King Kong' betrayal myth, Bedell Smith's warning, Major Brian Urquhart's reconnaissance photographs and General Browning, the landings of 17 September, Sepp Krafft's blocking line, John Frost at the Arnhem bridge, Viktor Gräbner's column, the blown bridge at Son and the intact bridge at Grave, Gavin and the Nijmegen bridge, the Waal crossing of the 504th, the four tanks at Lent, Hell's Highway, Sosabowski's Polish brigade at Driel, the Oosterbeek pocket and the withdrawal across the Rhine.

The defeat at Arnhem was avoidable — not by one heroic decision, but by any one of several the Allies never took.

In memory of the soldiers of all sides who fought along the road, and of the Dutch civilians who paid for it, including the victims of the Hunger Winter.

Disputed points, such as the 'bridge too far' remark and how much the four tanks at Lent could have changed, are presented as debated.
All scenes are animated illustrations, not archival footage.
